_purpose: The Product Backlog + Sprint Backlog (Scrum-inspired, adapted for AI-executed work -- see docs/interview-scenarios/ and the 2026-09-18 overnight design conversation for the full reasoning). Every non-trivial task Claude does gets an entry here, SIZED before work starts (Small/Medium/Large/XLarge -- the current official Scrum term is 'size', not 'estimate' -- Claude, the one doing the work, is responsible for sizing it, per the 2020 Scrum Guide's own principle) with a real numeric hour estimate + confidence (Phase 2, 2026-09-20). 'status' distinguishes Product Backlog (backlog) from Sprint Backlog (active) from done work. A 'sprint' here is NOT a fixed timebox -- it's the variable-length span of one OR MORE sized items approved together for one work session, start to finish (corrected 2026-09-20 from the original 'one sized item only' definition once a real multi-item sprint was tried in practice; see design rationale below). Retro is real and manual (docs/RETRO_LOG.md, Phase 2's estimation-calibration loop), proven to add real value across BL-007 and the BL-009-015 sprint before any scheduled/automated retro subagent is considered.

_sizing_rubric.SMALL: One clear sub-ask, one file or a tightly-scoped handful, follows an existing pattern in this codebase, low ambiguity. Attach a real numeric hour estimate (not just the label), even if narrow (e.g. 10-20 min).
_sizing_rubric.MEDIUM: A few distinct sub-asks or files, may touch 2 layers (e.g. backend + frontend), mostly follows existing patterns with some new logic. Attach a real numeric hour estimate.
_sizing_rubric.LARGE: Multiple sub-asks/files/subsystems, meaningful new logic or design decisions, real ambiguity requiring investigation before implementation. Attach a real numeric hour estimate; if the task is the FIRST real integration of a given kind in this codebase (first multi-service call, first use of a new infra piece, first cross-boundary flow), default to LARGE even if the individual steps sound simple -- unknown-unknowns are structurally higher the first time a pattern is exercised (real finding: BL-007 item 7, guessed MEDIUM, was actually LARGE for exactly this reason).
_sizing_rubric.XLARGE: Cross-cutting, genuinely novel (no existing pattern to extend), high ambiguity, likely spans multiple work sessions. For an XLARGE epic, size architecture/integration risk (drives confidence: LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) and per-component implementation effort (drives the hour range) SEPARATELY rather than one blended number -- do not let heavy code reuse from an existing proven pattern (porting/adapting, not designing fresh) hide inside a number calibrated for ground-up novel work. If the task is known up front to be splittable across independent parallel subagents, give TWO figures: a sequential-effort estimate and a parallelized-wall-clock estimate, since parallel execution collapses wall-clock time in a way a single sequential number will not predict.

_design_rationale: PHASE 1 (2026-09-18): a sized item is the natural 'sprint' unit, not a fixed clock, because there is exactly one executor working sequentially (no multi-person sync problem a fixed timebox exists to solve). Retro/correction was deliberately deferred to a later phase, to avoid the exact waste this system exists to prevent (an elaborate measurement system costing more than it saves). PHASE 2 (2026-09-20, built once Phase 1 proved real value on BL-007): the estimation-calibration loop (see _calibration_process below) and docs/RETRO_LOG.md now exist for real, and a 'sprint' was corrected the first time it was actually tested in practice -- a real multi-item sprint (7 items, approved together for one work session bounded by an elapsed-time target) showed the original 'one sized item = one sprint' definition was too narrow. A sprint is now one OR MORE sized items approved together for one work session, start to finish -- still not a fixed calendar clock, still no Daily-Scrum-style ceremony, since there is still exactly one executor.

items.title: Redis: distributed lock for contract-plan enrollment concurrency
items.description: Layered defense-in-depth over the existing uq_contract_plan_one_active_per_customer DB constraint: a short-TTL Redis lock (SETNX + Lua-script token-owned release, avoiding the classic 'delete someone else's lock after my TTL expired' bug) acquired before ContractPlanService.enroll()'s critical section, released only after the transaction commits (TransactionSynchronizationManager.afterCompletion, not a plain finally -- releasing earlier would reopen the exact race the lock exists to close). A losing request gets a clean 409 (EnrollmentInProgressException) instead of racing to the database and surfacing a raw 500. Graceful fallback when Redis is unreachable: proceed without app-level locking, relying solely on the DB constraint, same philosophy as ContractPlanCacheService.
items.size_rationale: New service (EnrollmentLockService) with a genuinely novel-to-this-codebase pattern (token-owned Lua-script release, transaction-synchronization-timed release), new exception + GlobalExceptionHandler mapping, 2 new test files including a real concurrent-threads integration test -- meaningful new design decisions, not pattern-following. items.title: Private engineering-memory & interview-evidence system V1
items.description: Owner-directed. Three levels: raw evidence (REFERENCED, not copied, from the existing event ledger/git/CI), verified learnings (new canonical ID-addressable records), and interview intelligence (curated, traceable to evidence). Three failures needed more than the prompt: (1) the model kept repeating the books' own audit register ('no genuine evidence'), fixed by a prompt rule that explicitly translates audit wording into speech; (2) it recited theory out of interview-prep excerpts as if it were memory, fixed by naming preparation material as not-memory; (3) the retry told only a violation CATEGORY swapped one banned phrase for another, fixed by quoting the matched words back. Editing a prompt and adding a regex list looks like known-pattern work, but the actual work was iterative convergence against a non-deterministic generator -- five prompt iterations, each needing a real model call to evaluate, each revealing a failure mode unpredictable from reading the code. The tell is whether the acceptance criterion can be evaluated WITHOUT running the model; if it cannot, the pattern is investigation_only.

_calibration_process._purpose: Phase 2 (added 2026-09-20, BL-007 retro): the estimation-calibration loop that makes sizing actually improve over time, adapted from Scrum for one AI executor + one human Product Owner. Every retro and its full data (comparison tables, verdicts, evidence, action items, discussion) is stored durably in docs/RETRO_LOG.md, never left only in chat.
loop: 1. Size a task before work starts (numeric hour estimate + confidence, not just the T-shirt label -- see _sizing_rubric).

3. Retro at the end of every sprint (one sized item, start to finish -- never a fixed calendar cadence): compare time required (estimate) vs. time taken (actual) using the tolerance band below. ALWAYS report the OVERALL sprint estimate vs. actual too, not just per-item numbers -- re-add the summed range from the individual items rather than trusting an earlier stated total (a real arithmetic slip happened once, 2026-09-20). When items ran in parallel, give both the summed-individual-duration figure and the real wall-clock figure, and say plainly that they answer different questions.

4. Any gap outside tolerance is diagnosed as exactly one of two causes (both may apply to the same item if real evidence supports both, named as two separate findings, never blended into a false single verdict): (a) ESTIMATION WRONG -- the size/estimate itself was miscalled, or (b) IMPLEMENTATION ISSUES -- the estimate was right but a real execution mistake cost extra time.

5. Action items are written from the diagnosis, WITHOUT sizing the action items themselves, in exactly THREE fixed sections every time (Owner's permanent structure, 2026-09-20): (1) estimation-mistake improvements with proper reasons, (2) implementation-mistake improvements with proper reasons, (3) items that are neither but still needed, with proper reasons. At least one item must address the SPRINT AS A WHOLE, not only individual tasks.
6. Wait for the Owner's explicit approval before touching anything for those action items -- this is a deliberate exception to the general autonomy-first default on this project.
7. Work the approved action items first, before picking up any new task.
8. Only then size the NEXT new task, using the updated rubric/knowledge -- never retroactively re-size an already-completed old task.

LESSON (BL-012, 2026-09-20 sprint): when two sprint items are planned to run concurrently and one plausibly produces a reusable artifact for the other, flag the later item's estimate as PROVISIONAL at plan time -- do not treat concurrently-run items as fully independent when sizing them.

LESSON (BL-013, 2026-09-20 sprint): before sizing a 'build X feature' task, verify whether X already exists (even partially) in the current repo state -- an estimate that assumes a green-field build when a skeleton already exists from an earlier session will run high for the wrong reason.

LESSON (BL-014, 2026-09-20 sprint): a LOW-confidence, first-of-its-kind integration task may validly conclude as a real, valuable PARTIAL (root cause found, not fully solved) rather than a finished result within its estimated range -- this is an honest, acceptable outcome of LOW confidence, not a process failure, and should be sized/communicated as such up front (the estimate range describes effort invested, not a promise of completion).

LESSON (2026-09-20 sprint, sprint-level): a multi-item sprint's summed estimate must flag which items are plannable as PARALLEL (independent files/directories, safe for a forked subagent) before work starts, and give both a summed-SEQUENTIAL figure and an expected WALL-CLOCK figure for the sprint as a whole -- not just for a single large epic (BL-007's own retro already required this at epic level; this sprint showed the same gap applies at sprint level across multiple independently-sized items).

LESSON, HIGH PRIORITY (2026-09-20, found via a rigorous ratio check across the BL-009-015 sprint, not just soft judgment): every completed item in that sprint landed at 0.09-0.68 of its estimate's midpoint -- NONE within the stated +-30% tolerance band. Two sprints in a row (this one and BL-007) show the same directional bias: hour-range estimates are still calibrated for a slower execution pace than this actual context (AI execution + heavy reuse of already-proven patterns in a codebase Claude already knows + real parallelization) delivers. ACTION: bias future numeric hour-range estimates meaningfully lower than intuition suggests, especially for tasks mirroring an existing proven pattern in this codebase (which should trend toward the LOW end of their size band, not the middle) -- and always compute the actual/estimate-midpoint RATIO explicitly at retro time rather than a soft 'did anything go wrong' judgment call, since the latter missed this same finding on 3 items the first time this sprint's retro was written.

CATEGORY TAGGING, STRICT RULE (2026-09-20, Owner directive): every backlog item carries a category -- 'delivery' (real sprint output/product work) or 'scrum_process' (sizing/retro/rubric/process-infrastructure work like BL-001 and BL-008). No item may lack a category, same discipline as size/estimate. Work that is not a sized backlog item at all (ad-hoc discussion/research between sprints) is tracked separately in docs/OUTSIDE_SPRINT_LOG.md with its own category (bookkeeping/research/discussion), not blended into this file's items. Purpose: let a future report compare real cost of SCRUM overhead itself against real cost of delivery work, to judge whether the overhead is worth it -- the Owner's own explicit goal.

PRE-SPRINT-PROPOSAL CHECKLIST, MANDATORY (2026-09-20, found via a real incident -- 4 rounds of Owner correction were needed before a sprint proposal actually reflected real priorities): before presenting ANY sprint proposal, explicitly check, in writing, against each of: (1) unfinished/active items from the previous sprint, (2) any standing recurring commitments made in prior conversation (e.g. once-per-sprint research tasks), (3) the most recently stated priorities in conversation, (4) real work items already sitting in docs/ACTION_QUEUE.json. Do not rely on memory/judgment alone to decide what belongs in a sprint -- the checklist is the check, not a formality. (5) ADDED 2026-09-20 after a real incident (Sprint 4: 3 of 12 items were sized as new work but were real duplicates of already-completed, undocumented work): for every docs/ACTION_QUEUE.json item being considered, do a real existence check before pricing it -- actually read the current implementation of the file/function/module the item references (not just a path-name grep, which is weak enough to produce false confidence on its own), and confirm the described gap genuinely still exists. (6) ADDED 2026-09-20: for every new item, run `python agent/backlog.py suggest-estimate <SIZE> <CONFIDENCE> <PATTERN_TYPE> "<raw range>"` (see agent/backlog.py's own docstring for PATTERN_TYPE values) and report its real output alongside the proposed number -- COMPUTED output with n>=3 is a real, historically-grounded suggestion to weigh seriously; INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY is an honest signal to fall back to the raw rubric band, not license to ignore the tool. A deviation from a COMPUTED suggestion must be stated explicitly with a real reason, never silently overridden. RETRO ACTION 2026-09-20 (BL-036 ratio 0.17), applied 2026-09-22: when an item spans N identical targets (N services, N files, N endpoints), the existence check must COUNT how many targets already satisfy the requirement and price only the remaining ones -- confirming the requirement isn't fully met somewhere is not enough.

Mid-sprint scope/understanding changes that Claude discovers on its own do NOT trigger a re-estimate -- finish the sprint as originally planned; the gap surfaces only in that sprint's normal retro and always counts as ESTIMATION WRONG (a self-realized sizing miss is by definition an estimation-logic gap, not an execution mistake). The ONLY thing that triggers a mid-sprint re-estimate is the Owner himself changing the scope mid-task -- re-size immediately when that happens, log why, then continue.
_calibration_process.tolerance: Starting band (set 2026-09-20, first version): actual-time / estimate-midpoint ratio within [0.7, 1.3] (+-30%) = matched, no gap. Outside that band triggers the full diagnosis in step 4. Tighten this band periodically (e.g. every ~10 retro'd items) as real variance narrows -- each tightening is itself a dated entry in docs/RETRO_LOG.md, since a shrinking tolerance band is the visible evidence the loop is working. REAL DATA POINT (2026-09-20): the first real multi-item sprint tested against this band showed a one-sided bias, not narrowing variance -- all 7 items ran fast (ratio 0.09-0.68), none slow. Do NOT symmetrically tighten the band in response to a one-sided bias like this -- that would not fix the real problem (estimates still calibrated too high) and would make the band asymmetrically punishing. The correct response to a one-sided bias is recalibrating the ESTIMATES lower (see the loop lesson above), not narrowing the tolerance window. Only tighten the band once real variance is seen clustering closer to 1.0 in BOTH directions.
_calibration_process.storage: docs/RETRO_LOG.md is the canonical, permanent store for every retro's full data -- see that file's own structure. This _calibration_process block is the mechanism; RETRO_LOG.md is the history.
_calibration_process.insufficient_history_rule_2026_09_27: RULE ADDED 2026-09-27 (Sprint 8 retro action 1): when suggest_estimate returns INSUFFICIENT_HISTORY, record estimate_range as the literal string 'NO RELIABLE ESTIMATE' and keep only the size label. Do NOT fall back to the raw rubric band and call it an estimate. Evidence: BL-079 was sized 5-8h from the rubric with n=0 and came in at ~32 min, a ratio of 0.08 -- a band with no reference class is a guess wearing a number, and it gets planned against as though it were data. SECOND, UNRESOLVED FINDING: even an ADOPTED COMPUTED suggestion is still running ~3x high (BL-078 ratio 0.30 against the engine's own 23.4 min midpoint). Applying the observed residual bias as a second factor inside suggest_estimate is a real pending change to agent/backlog.py, not yet implemented.
_calibration_process.residual_bias_factor_rejected_2026_09_27: TESTED AND REJECTED 2026-09-27 (Sprint 9): applying the observed residual bias as a second factor inside suggest_estimate, proposed by the Sprint 8 retro. Sprint 9 adopted the COMPUTED suggestions unmodified and both scoreable items landed ABOVE the band (ratios 1.9 and 3.3) -- the first over-estimates in the project's history. The engine's 0.16 median comes from sprints that over-estimated; feeding it into a correctly-sized task over-corrects. A second factor would have amplified this. Two sprints now show oscillation (0.30 under, then 1.9/3.3 over), not convergence. Do not re-propose this from the Sprint 8 text.

_calibration_fields._purpose: Added 2026-09-20 as a direct fix for a real, named root cause: four sprints of retro narrative had never been mechanically fed back into how the next estimate gets computed. These fields make that possible via agent/backlog.py's suggest_estimate() -- see CLAUDE.md's sizing discipline section.
_calibration_fields.actual_ratio: float or null. actual_duration / estimate_midpoint for this item, as already carefully computed and published in docs/RETRO_LOG.md's own retro tables -- transcribed here, not re-derived. null when no reliable ratio exists (pre-dates numeric estimation, or the item's own execution was too contaminated to produce one at all, e.g. BL-032).
_calibration_fields.pattern_type: one of: apply_known_pattern | first_of_kind | investigation_only | verification_only | research | unclassified. Classified from the item's OWN size_rationale text (written BEFORE the work started) or, for verification_only, from a real duplicate-work finding recorded in actual_note -- deliberately never chosen after the fact to match how long the item took, to avoid the exact bias risk a 2026-09-20 self-critique named directly.
_calibration_fields.contaminated: bool. true only when actual_note documents a real process failure (agent stall + takeover, a since-corrected wrong root-cause call, a combined-commit split that makes an isolated duration impossible) that makes this item's own ratio non-representative of normal execution. suggest_estimate() excludes contaminated=true items from its reference-class lookups.
_calibration_fields.contamination_reason: string, present only when contaminated=true -- the real, specific reason, never a bare boolean with no explanation.
